title: Hospitality
definition: Hospitality is the generous practice of welcoming, serving, and caring for others in the love of Christ.
summary: Hospitality uses what God has given to welcome and serve others.
christFocus: Jesus welcomed sinners, fed the hungry, received the outcast, and prepares a place for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Hospitality is more than entertaining friends. It is a Gospel-shaped welcome that uses home, time, resources, attention, and care for the good of others.

Scripture calls believers to practice hospitality without grumbling. This includes welcoming fellow believers, strangers, the lonely, the needy, and those who cannot repay.

Hospitality reflects the welcome of God in Christ. Believers who have been received by grace learn to make room for others.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people feel unseen, unwanted, or isolated. Hospitality matters because it turns love into tangible welcome and makes the care of Christ visible.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use what you have to welcome someone. Share a meal, make space, listen well, include the lonely, and serve without needing recognition or repayment.
